thread.en: It's definitely his fault for confidently refusing to buy a Mercurial Scimitar and getting picked off to cost his team the game, but you can't pin all the blame on him either. Caitlyn isn't just about mindlessly dragging things to the late game; picking Caitlyn is mostly about applying pressure and playing a tower-pushing tempo. T1 played great early on, aside from big O taking the first little drake a bit late, and they had a 3 to 4k gold lead by ten minutes. The turning point was that Baron. After taking that Baron, if they played it safe and pushed, they could've secured at least another couple thousand gold. With a Caitlyn comp and a 6k gold lead, they basically would've steamrolled. Instead, big O got caught first, and then Faker got caught mid. They took a Baron and somehow gave back 2k gold in the process. After that, DK wasn't scared of taking teamfights with T1 at all, and T1 became all timid. To sum it up, you can mindlessly play hypercarries and drag to the late game, but the catch is you have to cut down your error rate. Your macro has to be airtight without leaving openings, otherwise—unless the enemy team's scaling completely falls behind yours—it's super hard to rely purely on a single hypercarry ADC to solve all your problems.

top.en: I've figured it out: whenever T1's bot lane plays hyper-carries, their entire offensive tempo becomes as sluggish as constipation—long and smelly. They enter the game and just wait for the bot lane to scale. The problem is, you don't have the disciplined macro of Gen.G, and someone always steps up to throw the tempo. Then they wait for a late-game teamfight; if they win, they win, if they lose, it's GG. So, is it that T1's ADC can't play hyper-carries, or do you guys just not know how to play around them?
